content.text:
Micron Technology, Inc. Reports Record Fiscal Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year 2026 Results: The original earnings release reports fiscal Q4 GAAP gross margin of 86.8% and non-GAAP gross margin of 87.0%. This distinguishes actual Q4 results from the 86.25% Q1 gross-margin outlook in the prepared remarks. (time=2026-09-30; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Acer CEO says memory makers are hyping 2030 shortage fears to protect margins — PC prices set to decline by late 2027: Reporting Acer CEO Jason Chen's view, the article forecast PC-component prices reversing in the second half of 2027 as Chinese capacity came online; it also reported anticipated near-term PC price increases and a plateau in the first half of 2027. This is a competing OEM forecast, not a measured DRAM/NAND supply balance. (time=2026-09-21; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text:
Micron CEO says it'll be tougher to get memory in the next couple of years than it is today, and keeps saying it over and over again: The page reports Mehrotra's Q4-call warning that memory and storage conditions would be tighter in FY2027 and FY2028 than FY2026, and links to an Investing.com transcript. Search-result metadata gives a publication time before the supplied Tom's Hardware article; no dated archive of the page copy was found. (time=2026-10-01T10:13:59Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Micron projects tightening RAM shortages through 2028 as it generates record profit: The article reports Micron's forecast of tighter memory and storage supply-demand conditions in 2027–28, and says the company had sold most of next year's capacity at higher prices. Its supplied original text was captured at 12:52:28Z, before cutoff. The article's 86.25% figure is discussed as Q1 guidance later in its text; official materials clarify it was not actual Q4 margin. (time=2026-10-01T12:50:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text:
Fiscal Q4 2026 Earnings Call Prepared Remarks: Dated September 30, the remarks forecast memory and storage supply-demand conditions much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, with no line of sight to balance. Micron expected DRAM and NAND bit shipments to grow while industry supply remained constrained, and HBM shipments to grow faster than conventional DRAM. It also described the 86.25% gross-margin figure as Q1 FY2027 guidance. (time=2026-09-30; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Fiscal Q3 2026 Earnings Call Prepared Remarks: Micron's prior-quarter remarks expected tight conditions to persist beyond calendar 2027, attributing that outlook to AI-driven demand and structural supply constraints. The September statement therefore sharpened an existing tight-supply outlook rather than introducing it for the first time. (time=2026-06-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
